Main guide ↗

From the serve command to a ready model.

One continuous call tree combines QnA 1.1.1–1.1.6: CLI parsing, checkpoint configuration, architecture registration, tokenizer/defaults, model weights, graph compilation and HTTP readiness. Function links open complete original source; links labeled call site highlight the invoking line.

SOURCE · 610f7111836d9a950d45ba52ec9b3e0ed589fe3f · Standard API/worker path, one device, Graph API. Selected calls and illustrative values; no model execution was recorded. External APIs link to their MAX invocation.

# Explicit task: the task-inference branch is skipped.
max serve --model meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf --task text_generation

# Infer task: taken when the effective task is UNDEFINED (no config-file task).
max serve --model meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf

+-- call/branch · -> condensed call chain or labeled data flow · => process handoff · [ALIAS:L123] exact source location. The worker branch is a separate Python process. Repeated calls for new configuration objects and conditional lookups remain explicit.

Startup map · API process / Hub cache / model worker · SOURCE
SOURCE: startup order for the standard Llama 2 7B Graph API route

MAIN / API PROCESS               HF HUB / DISK CACHE          MODEL WORKER PROCESS
------------------------------   -------------------------    ------------------------------
Click loads options
  -> register lazy import map                                 (not started)
CLI builds PipelineArgs
  -> checkpoint probe ---------> config / generation files
  -> infer task if UNDEFINED
  -> build PipelineConfig
Registry prepares factory
  -> memory plan
  -> tokenizer ----------------> tokenizer assets
  -> deferred factory                                        (still not started)
FastAPI app -> Uvicorn Config
  -> Server object
Enter MAX lifespan
  -> telemetry + ZMQ interface
  -> spawn worker -----------------------------------------> reconstruct config; own HF cache
  |                                                          invoke model_factory()
  |                              weight files <------------- resolve paths / fetch misses
  |                                                          Llama3Config initialize/finalize
  |                                                          trace -> compile -> init graphs
  |                                                          warmup + queues + scheduler
  <- readiness Event --------------------------------------- alive.set()
  -> API proxy <============= ZeroMQ connection ============> worker queues
  -> yield lifespan
server.serve(): accept HTTP                                   scheduler loop

After startup: request/cancel -> worker; results -> API proxy -> HTTP client.
Cache hits may avoid downloads. Arrows show order/data flow, not measured durations.
